# Performance

## How to read this

- Every number comes from a committed run under `bench/results/<experiment>/<run-id>/`. All of these are real measurements on one machine; nothing in this file is simulated.
- The gateway, the load generator and the mock share one machine and talk over loopback. The mock's delays are configured constants, so absolute latencies are the mock's; only the difference between two paths measures a gateway.
- Latencies run from each request's scheduled time (open loop), so a slow response does not hide the requests queued behind it.
- Runs are chosen by `bench/results/SELECTION.yaml`; the primary overhead run and the first Linux run are both shown, with the reason.

#### Limitations of the measurement (copied from the run's report)

- One run per cell: there are no repetitions and no confidence intervals. A difference of a fraction of a millisecond is within the run-to-run noise of a shared machine.
- The generator, the gateway and the mock compete for the same CPU, and other programs on this machine could not be controlled. The launch lag table shows how much the generator itself added.
- The gateway writes one log line per request to a file; accounting, the decision log and tracing are off, and the tenant has no limits (see bench/configs/overhead.yaml).
- The server-side quantiles have the resolution of the histogram buckets (about a factor of 2.15 per bucket), so a p95 can be undecided against the target.
- The mock answers with constant delays and tiny bodies; real providers add variable latency, and larger bodies would cost the gateway more to copy.
- All requests carry one fixed short prompt.

#### Limitations of the measurement (copied from the run's report)

- One run per cell, no repetitions and no confidence intervals. A difference of a fraction of a millisecond is within the run-to-run noise of a shared machine.
- Linux under WSL2 in a VM that shares the host with Windows; the generator, the mock and the gateway compete for the same CPU. The launch lag table shows how much the generator itself added.
- LiteLLM's numbers depend on its worker count (8 here) and its settings; another count would give other numbers. Only this version and these settings were measured.
- The mock answers with constant delays and tiny bodies; real providers add variable latency, and larger bodies cost a gateway more to copy.
- All requests carry one fixed short prompt.
